Rick Doblin, founder of the Multidisciplinary Association for Psychedelic Studies, sits with Rogan for episode 1661 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Doblin has spent decades working to make MDMA and other psychedelics legal as medicines. Few guests know the drug-policy fight from as far back as he does.

He updates Rogan on clinical trials for PTSD and the long road through federal approval. The talk also covers how drug laws formed, why they stuck, and what legal therapy might look like. Doblin's calm, patient style makes the episode a clear map of where psychedelic medicine stood at that point.

Neuroscientist Bobby Azarian joins Joe Rogan for episode 1829 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Azarian wrote The Romance of Reality, which argues the universe trends toward knowledge and awareness. His work blends physics, biology, and philosophy into one big story.

Azarian lays out his view that life and mind are not accidents but central to how the cosmos works. He explains emergence, where simple parts build complex wholes with new powers. Rogan tests the ideas against evolution, AI, and free will. Curious and thoughtful listeners get science with soul, plainly said, from a young thinker with a grand theory.

Comic Kurt Metzger brings his rants to episode 2434 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Metzger, a writer for hit comedy shows and a fearless stand-up, is known for saying what others will not. His hour here is sharp, bitter, and funny in his trademark way.

Metzger fires off views on media, politics, and the comedy world's own rules. He and Rogan share stories of jokes that drew real backlash. The talk wanders into dark corners that network TV would never touch. Laughing and irreverent listeners get a comic who treats wrongthink as his whole act.

Comic Chris DiStefano tells Joe Rogan the story of being expelled from school on September 11 in this clip. DiStefano, a New York stand-up, was a class clown in a city school when the attacks came. His wild school days and that terrible day collide in one tale.

DiStefano recounts the trouble that got him thrown out and the chaos unfolding outside that same morning. He mixes grief, guilt, and comedy the way only a New Yorker of his age can. Rogan helps him tell it straight. Laughing and nostalgic listeners get a coming-of-age story set against a day no one forgets.
